outcome: Advise an unknown function or aggregate with the nearest accepted name or a raw_query first step, and add date_diff so differences between dates and timestamps are computed in semantic expressions.
criteria: date_diff(unit, start, end), also spelled datediff, resolves to an integer for date and timestamp operands with the unit validated, compiles to DuckDB date_diff, and a subtraction between temporal operands is refused with advice naming it.

An unknown scalar function is advised: a name close to an accepted one is rewritten to it, otherwise the refused step becomes a raw_query first step when it is the first normalized step, and the raw_query form is explained elsewhere; the rewrites run.
An unknown aggregate that picks one value per group (any_value, first, arbitrary) is rewritten to min with the reason stated, and any other unknown aggregate is explained with the raw_query form.
Tests on the example orders data and unrelated temporal data cover each case, fail without the change, and the full suite including the boundary tests passes.
The transform tool description and the README list date_diff and the new advice, and a pull request against Intentum main states the behaviour, tradeoffs and limitations.

note: date_diff(unit, start, end) added with unit validation, datediff and five other dialect names resolved as aliases with a note; temporal subtraction refused with a hint and temporal_difference advice. unknown_function: a close name is renamed outside literals, otherwise the first normalized filter or derive becomes a raw_query first step, elsewhere explained; unknown_aggregate: any_value/first/arbitrary become min, others explained. 4 new tests fail without the change; 394 passed. Of the 24 recorded refusals of these kinds in an agent run, 3 now resolve, 9 get temporal_difference, 3 get the min rewrite and 9 the raw_query advice. The PR is opened after this commit.
